infra-context · generated 2026-10-11

Infra map

How Bunkai is built, run and deployed. Source of truth: ../upex-bunkai-tms at origin/staging (98ee1b4, 2026-10-11). Paths are relative to that repo unless they start with .context/ of this QA repo.

Overview

Pattern: feature-based modular monolith. One Next.js 15 app holds the UI (app/(app)/**) and the REST API (app/api/v1/**); domain logic sits in per-feature folders under lib/<domain>/ (37 folders). Business invariants live in Postgres bunkai_* RPC functions that raise custom 45xxx SQLSTATEs; each domain's errors.ts maps them to API errors. The RPC, not a service class, is the unit of business logic.

Deployment shape: a single serverless deployable on Vercel; staging branch to the staging environment, main to production. Local, staging and production all use the SAME Supabase project (fmbpikzpkafptqximhxn), so there is no environment-level data isolation.

Containers and data flow

  1. Browser or agent sends HTTPS to the Vercel deployment.
  2. middleware.ts refreshes the Supabase session cookie on every non-static path and redirects to /login?next=… for the protected prefixes /home, /projects, /onboarding, /settings, /activity when there is no user.
  3. API calls hit withApiHandler: it resolves the caller (resolveIdentity), checks the route's declared capabilities, runs the handler, attaches x-request-id and writes one structured log line.
  4. The domain module validates with Zod and calls a bunkai_* RPC through an RLS-scoped Supabase client; SQLSTATEs map to the error envelope { error: { code, message } }.
  5. Long work runs outside the request: Jira import and workspace export in Vercel after() with the service-role client; the run inactivity sweep and the workspace purge inside Postgres via pg_cron; the email digest via Vercel Cron to /api/v1/admin/send-digest.
  6. Inbound third-party calls: Stripe posts to /api/v1/billing/webhook. Outbound: Jira REST (import), Stripe API (checkout), Resend (digest), Supabase Realtime pushes run updates to the Runner view.

Auth flow

  1. Interactive sign-in through Supabase Auth: password, magic link, or OAuth (GitHub, Google). The session lives in an SSR cookie (sb-<project-ref>-auth-token).
  2. Headless sign-in: POST /api/v1/auth/signin returns the cookie and, optionally, a freshly minted PAT (detail in backend).
  3. A PAT (Authorization: Bearer bk_pat_…) is verified by hash; the server mints a short-lived user JWT per request so RLS sees the same auth.uid() as a cookie session.
  4. Both paths collapse into one Principal (lib/api/principal.ts, product ADR-0001).

Database

One Supabase Postgres project for all environments. App access goes through PostgREST/RPC with the caller's JWT (RLS enforced); the service-role client (RLS bypassed) is reserved for the idempotency ledger, PAT secrets and the background workers. QA inspection uses DBHub with the read-only role qa_inspector_ro through the session pooler (grants maintained by migrations 0085, 0086, 0088). Subsystems: tenancy and RBAC, authoring (modules, stories, ACs), ATC library, tests and runs, defects, reporting, test plans and milestones, notifications, billing, workspace lifecycle (export, deletion), platform plumbing (idempotency, flags). Tables and lifecycles belong to business-data-context (still a placeholder); terms are in business-domain-context.

Security architecture

  • Authorization: RLS keyed to workspace_members.role is the only tenant-isolation boundary, validated by lib/api/rls-parity.test.ts.
  • Route posture: every route declares public, cookie-only (with a reason), authenticated (with a reason) or required with a non-empty capability list; an ungated route does not type-check.
  • Capabilities: atc:read, atc:write, run:execute, workspace:admin. Cookie sessions hold all; a PAT holds its minted subset and is bound to its workspace.
  • Cookie-only surfaces: workspace data export refuses PATs; billing checkout returns a distinguishable PAT rejection (BK-828).
  • Principal classes: cookie session, PAT, plus a system principal (CRON_SECRET) for the digest route and the Stripe signature for the webhook.
  • Secrets: lib/env.ts validates env with Zod behind a server-only guard; only NEXT_PUBLIC_* reach the browser. PAT secrets stored as SHA-256 hashes.
  • Non-disclosure: "not found" and "not a member" return the same response on bugs, runs, ATCs and deleted workspaces.

Performance hooks

  • Per-instance 60 s memo for the Home coverage rollup (lib/home/constants.ts, lib/home/coverage.ts); not shared across serverless instances.
  • /api/openapi is force-static with max-age=300.
  • Cursor pagination, 50 per page on bugs, run history and reports.
  • No general API rate limiter in code; see nfr-performance.

ADRs

No new test-architecture ADR seeded in this phase. Product-side decisions cited above live in the target repo's own .context/ADR/ (ADR-0001 unified auth, ADR-0005 PAT workspace scope, ADR-0012 RPC authorization, ADR-0015 workspace deletion, ADR-0017 cron principal).

QA relevance

  • Every mutating test needs an RLS negative case (other workspace, lower role).
  • Cookie and PAT must behave the same on required routes; cookie-only routes must refuse a PAT.
  • Each domain's errors.ts enumerates its negative SQLSTATEs: a ready list of negative cases.
  • Shared Supabase project: test data must be workspace-scoped and cleaned up.
  • Background work (sweep, purge, export, import, digest) needs polling or direct DB checks, not request/response asserts.

Stripe: checkout inserts its session row before calling Stripe (the row id is the client_reference_id), allows one open session per workspace, and dedupes webhook events by Stripe event id. Tests must use Stripe test mode and cover a replayed webhook and a double-tab checkout.

Resend: one digest log row per user per day (pending, sent, failed); a failed send is visible in that table, not to the user.

Jira: a missing or bad credential surfaces as a failed Import Job, not a boot error; the client backs off on 429 honoring Retry-After.

Database setup

Shared remote Supabase project; supabase/ holds only migrations/ (no config.toml, no seed.sql), so there is no local Dockerized stack. No migrate/seed npm script; db:qa-roles provisions the QA inspector roles; types:gen regenerates Supabase types.

Auth flow (concrete contract)

  1. POST /api/v1/auth/signin with { email, password, pat_name?, pat_scopes?, pat_expires_in_days? }.
  2. 200 sets the cookie sb-<project-ref>-auth-token and returns { user, session, pat: { token, scopes }, warning }; the PAT has the form bk_pat_<prefix>.<secret>.
  3. Unconfirmed accounts go through signup (email OTP) then confirm, which mints session + PAT.
  4. UI requests rely on the cookie (refreshed by middleware.ts); API requests accept the cookie or Authorization: Bearer bk_pat_….
  5. Cookie-only endpoints (workspace data export) reject a PAT.

The SUT's own /qa page (app/qa/qa-config.ts) documents the same endpoints with placeholders; it agrees with the code on the routes above.

Test-ID strategy

data-testid in kebab-case, purpose-named (tokens-list, tokens-empty, issue-token-open), often paired with ARIA roles; present in 99 files under components/ and app/. Prefer getByTestId over CSS or text.

Login test ids (from /qa, confirmed in the email-first login): login-email, login-continue, login-password. Gotcha: login-email also exists in the magic-link form, so once that toggle opens the locator matches two nodes and Playwright strict mode fails; scope by form.

Known findings

  • metadataBase hardcoded to http://localhost:3000 in app/layout.tsx: OG URLs misresolve on staging and production.
  • No error.tsx boundary anywhere; one not-found.tsx.
  • No sitemap, robots or manifest; no bundle analyzer; no Web Vitals tooling.
  • /workspaces/[id]/members is gated by a page-level redirect, not by the middleware prefixes.

Default QA target: staging (this repo's .agents/project.yaml, testing.default_env). bunkai.io and bankai.io are declared domains, not live hosts.

Per-environment variables

Only NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL is known to differ. Supabase URL and keys point at the same project (fmbpikzpkafptqximhxn) everywhere, so staging writes land in the production database.

Secrets, cloud, monitoring, rollback

  • Secrets: Vercel environment variables; local .env. No vault, no rotation policy documented.
  • Cloud: Vercel (hosting, Cron), Supabase (Postgres 17.6, Auth, Realtime, Storage bucket for exports, pg_cron), Stripe, Resend.
  • Scheduled jobs: Vercel Cron daily 08:00 UTC to the digest route; pg_cron run sweep and workspace purge inside Postgres.
  • Monitoring: none beyond Vercel function logs; health endpoint is not polled by anything in the repo.
  • Rollback: Vercel redeploy of a previous deployment; migrations are forward-only, with no down scripts.
  • QA DB access: DBHub, read-only qa_inspector_ro, session pooler port 5432.

CI/CD

Server-side CI: none. No .github/workflows/, GitLab, CircleCI or Jenkins config. Vercel's own next build is the only check between push and deploy. No IaC, no Docker.

Local gates (Husky, bypassable)

# pre-commit
bunx lint-staged
bun run types:check
bun run vars:check
bun run skills:check
# (+ skills:registry:check when skill files are staged)

# pre-push
bun run format:check && bun run lint:check && VARS_ENV_CHECK_DRIFT=warn bun run vars:env:check \
  && bun run skills:registry:check && bun scripts/openapi-gen.ts --check && bun run agents:compat:check

bun test runs in no hook, not in repo:check, and in no CI. The 199 test files run only by hand.

Deploy

Vercel Git integration: push to staging deploys staging, push to main deploys production. vercel.json carries only the cron. Migrations are applied outside the deploy (not scripted in the repo).

Where QA automation runs

The SUT has no pipeline to hook into. This QA repo carries its own GitHub Actions workflows (.github/workflows/: build, smoke, sanity, regression) that run the KATA suites against the deployed staging URL; /regression-testing owns them.

Discovery gaps

  • Rate limits (NFR-PERF-004): unknown whether anything outside the code (Vercel firewall, Supabase gateway) enforces the documented numbers.
  • Security headers (NFR-SEC-006): Vercel platform defaults not measured against staging.
  • Stripe key mode on staging (test vs live) not verified.
  • Run inactivity threshold value and the pg_cron schedules' exact timing not extracted (in 0075 and 0084).
  • Product ADRs (ADR-0001, 0005, 0012, 0015, 0017) cited, not read in full this pass.
  • Password hashing and TLS inherited from Supabase Auth and Vercel; not verifiable from code.
  • Tier retention (30 / 90 days) has no pruning job; whether that is intended is unconfirmed.
  • Vercel environment-variable scopes and preview-deployment behaviour not verified (no dashboard access).
  • How migrations reach the shared database (Supabase CLI, dashboard, MCP) is not scripted in the repo.
  • No runtime version pin; local vs Vercel Bun/Node drift is undetectable from the repo.
  • Supabase region, backups and pooling for app writes not documented in the repo.
  • .env.example drift (wrong Supabase key names, missing Stripe, Resend-digest and cron keys): worth reporting to the dev team.
  • Production reachability not tested in this pass.
